cards.title: Today’s vocabulary
sections: excuse me · /ɪkˈskjuz mi/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
used politely to get attention or before interrupting someone. Excuse me. Is this your book?
I am sorry · /aɪ əm ˈsɑri/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
used to apologize when you have done something wrong. I am sorry. I have your pen.
could you help me · /ˌkʊd ju ˈhɛlp mi/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a polite way to ask another person for help. Could you help me with this word?
what does it mean · /ˌwʌt dəz ɪt ˈmin/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a question asking for the meaning of a word or expression. I can read this word. What does it mean?
I do not know · /aɪ du nɑt ˈnoʊ/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
used to say that you do not have the answer or information. Where is his book? I do not know.

articulation.label: help
articulation.alt: help: /h/ → /ɛ/ → /l/ → /p/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /h/: Gentle breath; mouth prepares for the vowel.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
/p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Read and write
sections: Reading

Puck wants help with a word. “Excuse me. Could you help me?” he asks Heart. He points to a word and asks, “What does it mean?” Heart says, “I do not know. Let us ask the teacher.” Puck sees that he has Heart's pen. “I am sorry,” he says, and gives it back.
Find the answer
What do they do when Heart does not know the meaning?
Write
Write two sentences using two words from today’s new word bank.
